name: Prairie Town
note: Prairie Town is fictional. Its plants, sizes and prices are illustrative. Hourly demand, wind and solar follow the shapes of real days on the Southwest Power Pool grid (town_year.json and town_days.json, from EIA-930), scaled down to the town.

dataset.creator: Honglin Li
dataset.status: Illustrative: Prairie Town, its plants, sizes and prices are fictional.
dataset.source: Illustrative fleet assumptions shared by lesson 0 and the lessons built on it.

units.mw: MW (plant size, or average output over an hour)
units.cost: $ per MWh (running cost: fuel and other costs that grow with output)
units.co2: t CO2 per MWh (t = metric tonne, 1,000 kg); illustrative operating emissions only: fuel burned at the plant. Construction, fuel supply and upstream methane are outside the boundary

lesson0.about: Lesson 0: one real late-summer day, scaled. The day is read from town_year.json by local date (Central daylight time, UTC-5; index i is the hour ending at start_utc + i). Demand = shape x demandPeakMW; wind and solar = shape x farm size (SPP's highest hour of 2025 = the farm at full output), rounded to whole MW; demand then rounded by at most 2.5 MW so that the gas needed each hour is a multiple of `step` (a careful player can balance exactly). Chosen on 2026-11-02 from June-September 2025 for a real midday solar dip (14:00-15:00, SPP solar 737 -> 553 -> 730 MW) and an evening climb faster than the combined-cycle plant's ramp limit.
